To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the local density of conspeci- fic plants had significant effects on individual reproductive success, as well as on total seed production.
the density of conspeci- fics within 1 m of a plant affects individual reproductive success and that high-density plants produce more seeds than otherwise similar low-density plants.

individual reproductive success, as mea- sured by seeds per fruit (SPF), proportion of flowers setting fruit (PFSF), and total seed production (TSP) increased with the density (number of plants within 1 m) of conspecifics for an insect-polli- nated desert mustard (Les querella fendleri).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of density on reproductive success and the role of density in mediating the effect of rarity on reproduction.
the role of density dependence and facilitation on reproductive success.
the effects of density on reproductive success in a desert mustard, Lesquerella fendeleri.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the density of conspecif- ics in the immediate vicinity of plants (1 m) had significant positive effects on reproductive success, whereas the density of conspecies at greater distances had little or no effect.
the density of conspeci- fic plants has an effect on the reproduction of L. fendleri, but that it is not the only factor that affects reproduction and that other factors are important as well.
density of conspeci- fics within 1 m of individual plants is positively correlated with reproductive success in L. fendleri.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the effects of plant rarity are complex and depend on a range of factors including the spatial and temporal scale of the study.
plant density has important effects on the reproductive success of a rare plant, but these effects occur on a small scale (i.e., within 1 m).

the density of conspeci- fic plants within a distance of about 1 m is an impor- tant determinant of reproductive success for L. fendleri and that this effect is probably caused by increased pollin- ator visitation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the effects of plant rarity on reproduction are complex, and that it is necessary to understand the spatial scales at which these effects occur.
density of conspecific plants can have important effects on individual reproductive success in a desert mustard and that the effects are not simply due to increased pollinator visit- tation.
plant density should be considered in studies of the effect of rarity on reproductive output.
